thread:
jin: quick q — should the onboarding pipeline run the full bench (1000+ inputs) for every new docker image build or only on tagged releases? saw a false negative yesterday where quantized model passed smoke but flaked on long-seq perf

olga: my vote: smoke on build, full bench on tag. builds are too noisy and slow for CI. smoke should catch obvious mismatches (tokenizer, model crash, shape errors).

mike: +1. but we need a better smoke suite — current 10 inputs missed a kv-cache mismatch. maybe a stratified sample: short/medium/long + a couple edge tokens.

jin: agreed. the flake was a kv-cache misalignment that only appeared after ~512 tokens. smoke didn't include long seq.

tara: what about intermediate canaries? e.g., run a medium bench on 'release-candidate' tags and schedule full bench overnight for main releases. saves cycles.

sam: suggestion: add a deterministic permutation of 20 golden prompts that cover tokenizer quirks, long prefix, function-calling shapes, and repeat tokens. store hashes of outputs for fast exact-match smoke. if hashes differ -> escalate to bench.

mike: hashes are brittle across quantization and minor nondet ops. we can use similarity thresholds (emd/embedding cosine) for semantic checks plus token-level canonical tests where determinism is expected.

jin: good point. maybe two-tier checks: 1) syntactic canonical tests (token ids, shapes, no exceptions) 2) semantic regressions (embedding cosine / n-gram overlap) with thresholds per model-family.

olga: and surface perf guardrails: if median latency on smoke > 2x baseline -> mark for full bench. often quantized kernels blow up perf for long seqs.

ops-bot: deploy-check: image 0x7a3 built by ci-42 triggered smoke-suite at 1723456789. Result: PASSED (smoke). Queued full-bench for tag v0.3.1.

tara: interface boundary question — should the onboarding pipeline live in eng-ml repo (closer to model tests) or eng-runtime infra (closer to resources and kernels)? current break causes duplicated docker sanity logic.

mike: keep orchestration and infra hooks in eng-runtime, but keep model-specific tests and sample sets in eng-ml as a package/artifact. then eng-runtime calls eng-ml artifacts via a versioned test-bundle.

sam: packaging idea: publish a small tarball with tests + golden prompts + metadata (expected tokenizer, acceptable similarity thresholds, warmup sequence lengths). include a manifest that runtime can parse:

```
model-test-manifest:
  model: redwood/opt-6b
  tokenizer: sentencepiece-v2
  smoke_set: s3://eng-ml/smoke/opt-6b/2026-02-01.tar.gz
  thresholds:
    embed_cosine: 0.92
    token_match_rate: 0.98
  perf_baseline: perf-id-2026-01-11
```

jin: pact sounds nice. also need clear fallback policy: if full bench fails after tag -> mark model quarantined and route runtime to fallback compatible variant (smaller or float32) automatically. Ops must get paged for persistent failures.

olga: agree. add an auto-rollforward: if latest tagged build fails bench for >2 consecutive tags, block that model-family until manual review.

mike: one more: test isolation. run tests in a deterministic CPU/GPU environment container (pinned CUDA/cuDNN). Many flakes are due to driver/kernel mismatches not model code. record environment fingerprint with results.

tara: actionable next steps:
- eng-ml: assemble stratified smoke set (20-30 prompts) + manifest schema (sam)
- eng-runtime: implement smoke gating logic & baseline perf comparisons (mike)
- infra: schedule nightly full benches for main branch and tagged releases (ops)
- oncall: define alerting thresholds for bench regressions (olga)

jin: thanks. i'll PR a starter manifest schema and example smoke tarball later today. will @everyone when ready :thumbsup:

ops-bot: note: queued job 7824 for full-bench; ETA ~4h.

sam: lgtm. keep an eye on tokenizer versioning — that's where most silent incompatibilities hide.
